Fantastic concept that's rarely attempted, and certainly not to this degree of quality. Tight gameplay mechanics, an uplifting soundtrack and atmosphere galore. The most fun I've had playing a video game this year.

Really nice game. Nice upgrade path and always something to strive for. 
I just hope there will be a DLC in the future!

This game is brutal, but also very fun and rewarding. If you like a challenge, and love shooters, and you love Zelda, you'll love this game! It's very well done. Also, there's an easy mode, which I haven't tried, but if the difficulty is deterring you, just do easy mode and you should be fine.

Love this game. I know it was only made by two people but man would it be great if there were save points and fast travel points in the overworld. The map is divided into chunks that you find. Maybe a save/fast travel point per mad chunk? I would 100% this game if there was. As it stands it sucks that you die you are sent back to the middle of town. Just going to do the main missions and call it.

Oh and why does this game not have i-frames when you boost? Even games like Dark Souls have i-frames.

Edit: Also Boss fights are too fucking long. Either give a heart between each stage or less stages. Still liking this game but some things are making me like it less.
Feels like a classic RPG from my childhood, with the added bonus of being a sch'mup, one of my favorite genres. Not too much in the way of story, but the mechanics are very solid if a bit simple.

I play and try a lot of games and not one of those ppl that plays for 20-30min and acts like can give a review. IMO dont give a review unless played minimum of 1-2 HR. I didnt think trailer was like I got to play this but reviews were great so tried the demo. played until finished and bought immediately full version. This game is a ton of fun. great pace of upgrades etc and always have something to do. Also plays very smooth and graphics are great also. Great work devs on what games r supposed to be . . . . fun. I work and raise my son alone so dont spend all day messing around on a pc. wouldnt if could though. But this game is great. sure any1 that tries will love it.

UPDATE: just finished the game and is probably the most fun I have had with a game in over a year, and I try alot of them and own alot if look at my games owned list. Really enjoyed this one. Thanks devs.

Twin-stick shmup/shooter and Original NES Legend of Zelda. How in the hells do those two genres work together? Well, I'll be damned, but they do. This game is absurdly fun and addictive, and worth the money.

I loved what this offered. Still playing and almost completed 100% but this was like playing Zelda as a child but mindful for adults. Plus, the twin stick shooter style gameplay is a perfect combination! Since there's also no violence I would also recommend for children that are starting to game with parental supervision since some of the puzzles while not overly difficult could provide some good learning opportunities. Played on a Dual Sense controller while didn't take advantage of the haptic features, the rest of the functions worked fine.

A Damn good game.

Pros:
+ Great exploration, many caves and minor dungeons to find and clear out
+ Pacing of new abilities/opening up of the map is well done
+ Level system is fantastic: respecing is available from the first level-up wherever and whenever you want to try new things
+ Bosses and enemies are well designed, memorable patterns stand out
+ Tons of secrets on a rather large map, magically feels smaller by the end to help collect the final few secrets
+ Surprisingly nice story
+ Cute friends!

Mehs:
~ Some upgrades feel pointless, are best used as crystal holders till you have enough for damage, range, and attack speed
~ The fourth main dungeon is a letdown, but is intriguing in its mystery

Cons:
- The final two main dungeons feel less than good, the first three dungeons are the standouts
- My friend said it looked like a newgrounds game, in a somewhat negative tone

Overall, I recommend this one.

Minishoot’ Adventures is a blast. The two-person studio behind it brilliantly marries old-school Legend of Zelda exploration with twin stick shooter gameplay—and it works exceedingly well. I’m not sure what sorcery they used here to pull off relaxing exploration with intense bullet hell.

Minishoot’ Adventures’ gameplay is fluid and its controls are very responsive. Each ability unlocked is meaningful but the game remains consistently challenging and rewarding, particularly the boss encounters. It doesn’t hurt that the game has a pleasant and dreamlike visual style. The sound design may be overlooked but deserves a lot of praise. I’m having a difficult time describing it but it’s charming and scratches an itch in my brain.

I highly recommend Minishoot’ Adventures and hope it inspires copycats.

absolutely fantastic, it's rare that I want to review a game before finishing it, but this takes the best elements of each of it's inspirations and creates something truly unique with it. It has the dungeon crawling from zelda, it has great metroidvania progression, and the bullet hell combat is extremely fun. This game is what I wish The knight witch would've been, tons of fun

This is one of those games that seems so obvious when you see it that you'll be asking yourself why you didn't think of it first. It plays a lot like you'd expect based on the description of a Zelda-like twin stick shooter and it's well made and challenging. If you have any interest in the top down style Zelda games or twin stick shooters I say it's worth trying.

EDIT after beating: Beat the game and it took me a little under 12 hours. I wish it was longer but the 12 hours really flew by and it felt like a lot less.

I'd also say the game is challenging but not quite challenging enough.
A short 30-minute test drive for this game quickly became a whole afternoon's gameplay. Incredibly addicting and polished game. 10/10 highly recommended.

Fantastic game for the steam deck if you like bullet hell games with meta-progession. Can get quite challenging at times but there are savepoints near major encounters, so you don't feel like there is time wasted.

Just like everyone says, it's Zelda bullet hell... but it IS super fun and addictive. 
Absolutely worth it for the price.

I thought I was mad because all I could think of was the SNES Zelda when playing, then I read the reviews. Not just me then.

It's superb, just buy it

Superb little gem, that simply fullfills the core premise of every game: just being fun. 

Exploration is fun and rewarding, because every item you find is significant, as are the skill points, which makes leveling up or -if necessary- grinding meaningful as well. Combat is tight and fair, albeit quite easy: even on the highest difficulty I was mostly breezing through encounters, safe for a few random difficulty spikes. Gradually learning new offensive and defensive skills means it never gets boring (also thanks to the perfect runtime).
Progression overall feels very satisfiying, starting from carefully and slowly moving room to room and taking your time with the enemies, to breezing over the whole map in an instant, destroying and dodging on your way.

Overall a very well-crafted metroidvania reminiscent of old Zelda-titles.

Great, fun, unique type of Metroidvania. Lots of challenging boss fights and cool secrets. Even 100%ing it is fun and not tedious.

If you like Twin-Stick shooters, bullet hells and exploration, you should try it. It's relatively short too. (8ish hours to finish story, 12ish hours to 100%)

There is a few points in the game where it's not very obvious what I have to do because it's very easy to miss a very tiny "hidden" spot in middle of nowhere, but other than that it is quite fun game.
Great combination of dungeon crawling and twin-stick shooter, with plenty of challenge, lots of places to explore, and some cool post-game content. Would absolutely love DLC or a sequel!

Honestly, I am so glad I found out about this game because it's wonderful. Everything I love rolled into one, with bullet-hell shooters, old school Zelda and Metroidvania style progression in a fun package. Really a fantastic little game that has lots to offer. I can't recommend it more and I hope we have a sequel in the works!

Its definitely one of the most unique MVs ive ever played and its utterly addicting. I think its absolutely worthy of the hype. Is it in my top 5...meh no but top 10 for sure. Others though might easily have it in their top 5 and I see why. Id say its around 6 or 7 for me though for sure. Anyways, buy it.
Seriously good time. Amazing visuals and great pacing, Just enough challenge to keep you trying but never unfair like some games with bullet hell bosses. Love this one
super fun, mixes dungeon crawler vibes with a charming twin stick shooter. Love the art style, mechanics, and controls.
Super cool game, I had a lot of fun with it! Plays super smoothly, has a great soundtrack and a satisfying reward system.
Fun game, a little bit on the easy side, but it is still a good time. Congrats to the devs.

It's a lot of content, and though I am playing on Advanced from the start (I'd recommend for gamer's), it's a good challenge but balanced. You lose enough, but then you win, and it feels real good. It's everything I hoped it would be and more! What a delightful adventure! I'll update more as I play further.

Edit: I have played further and the game just gets better and better. It's a rare thing when you're so excited for a game to come out and then it ends up being better than you hoped it would be. Great job SoulGame! had no idea how much I wanted a fusion of first Zelda game and a twin-stick shooter until just now. This game is fantastic. I can tell already that my biggest complaint is going to be that I wish there was more.

Edit 2: I have finished the game. This one will be on my top games of the year list, no doubt. It's everything I hoped it would be.

Minishoot' Adventures masterfully blends the exploration of classic Metroidvania titles with the intense action of twin-stick shooters. As a nimble spaceship, players navigate a meticulously crafted world filled with interconnected areas, uncovering secrets and upgrades that enhance both combat and traversal abilities. The game's design encourages curiosity, rewarding players who venture off the beaten path with valuable discoveries.

The combat system stands out with its responsive controls and escalating challenges. Encounters range from skirmishes with diverse enemy types to intricate bullet-hell boss battles that test reflexes and strategy. The progression system allows for meaningful customization, enabling players to tailor their ship's capabilities to their preferred playstyle.

Critics have lauded Minishoot' Adventures for its innovative genre fusion. God is a Geek praised it as "a fantastic twin-stick twist on the classic Zelda formula," highlighting its compelling gameplay and design. citeturn0search2 Similarly, The Verge recognized it among the standout indie games of the summer, noting its successful blend of bullet-hell shooting with Zelda-style adventuring. citeturn0news12

For fans of Metroidvania games or those seeking a fresh and engaging experience, Minishoot' Adventures offers a delightful journey that combines nostalgic elements with modern gameplay mechanics. Its harmonious balance of exploration and combat ensures that players remain captivated from start to finish.
This game blends 2D zelda and twin stick shooter in a tight 8 hour adventure. Fantastic!
Cute aesthetic, interesting world, lots of secrets. The gameplay is tight, the puzzles aren't frustrating. Just a good time from start to finish.
had a great time with this game. would love to see even more stuffs added to this game (maybe an expension pack)
This game is fun and addictive. It has features that allow you to adjust the difficulty, so you can play without feeling stressed. I love playing this game on the sofa with my Steam Deck.

A fantastic little game with absolutely stunning exploration and level design. It’s so intricate, constantly creating shortcuts to make exploring this world so seamless and fun. The progression is strong too with impactful upgrades that enhance both the movement and combat systems.

My only real issue with this game is how unlocking the ability to traverse on water undercuts the awesome level design. Whilst successfully expanding exploration (as it's intended to do), it simultaneously makes traversal less engaging because the map effectively becomes open world. In this transition, the level design loses the meticulousness that makes the early-to-mid-game so enthralling.

I highly recommend this to anyone interested, particularly if you like exploration-heavy experiences and/or twin-stick shooters in general.

Loved the time I spent with Minishoot' Adventures! I highly recommend for anyone who has played the 8-bit or 16-bit Zelda games; there's a lot of fun references sprinkled throughout. The music, controls, graphics, and gameplay are solid 🪨
Simple but great gameplay with 10+ hours of fun. This indie mix between Zelda and a twin stick shooter is highly recommended.

Enjoyable, fun and well balanced from start to end.

Hope to see a sequel or another game with the same gameplay loop found here.

Wow, I did not expect to find such a gem in this game. I really hope they make a sequel for I was absolutely absorbed by it for the around 8 hours that it took me to 100% it. If you like bullet hells and metroidvania-like progression, you'll feel right at home here. The controls are extremely tight, the upgrades are fantastic, and the quality of the content was superb. Honestly, if it goes straight to my top 10 of 2025. My only complain was the lack of a true ending final boss and perhaps a slightly better soundtrack.

4.5/5 - a MUST.

Despite how smooth the design is, rewarding the exploration, and exacting the dual-stick shooting, I admit I felt under-motivated to really just spend time in the world of Minishoot’ Adventures. Most of that is because I’m vain and petty. The art and name don’t do it for me. Griping aside, this game undeniably punches above its weight and as a game developed by two devs, it does deserve a ton of credit. Any other day this would be a clear nine out of ten game for me, but I’m giving it four stars ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ out of five.

Hopefully if you read this review, it just sets your expectations so that you’re really primed to fall in love with it.

(Minishoot’ Adventures, PC only)
Lovely little Zelda-like that excels at exploration. The pacing is smoothly brisk throughout the adventure. Highly recommend based on its tight-knit and well-explored premise.

Minishoot' Adventures is a perfect game. It's a delightful fix of Zelda and metroidvania in a tight 10 hour bullet-hell riddled package. It's beautiful, has good music, fantastic sound effects, plays precisely, has clean graphic design, fun bosses, a well constructed world with secrets and challenges, and ultimately gives you everything you could want from it. It's an easy 10/10.
